stem.en: A boulder on a hillside has a crack. Water freezes in the crack each night until the boulder falls into three pieces. All three pieces lie where they fell, next to each other. What has happened?

text.en: Erosion only, because the pieces came apart.

feedback.en: Coming apart is not erosion. Erosion needs the material to be carried away.

text.en: Both, because the boulder is now smaller.

feedback.en: The rock broke, but nothing carried the pieces away, so erosion has not happened.

text.en: Weathering only, because nothing was carried away.

feedback.en: Right. The rock broke down and the pieces stayed where they fell.

text.en: Neither, because the pieces are still on the hillside.

feedback.en: Weathering does not need movement. Breaking down in place is exactly what weathering is.

explanation.en: Frost broke the rock, which is physical weathering. Weathering does not involve movement of the broken material. Erosion would begin only if water, wind or ice carried the pieces away.

hints.en: Ask one question: did anything carry the pieces away?
